claims.statement: Every generated organizing artifact — sidecars, salience digests, connection suggestions, navigation surfaces, capture triage, and the daily review — is emitted through the proposal queue as a review-gated pull request rather than a direct write, and the agent never merges.

The proposal queue reuses the kernel safety surface — the protected-path guard and allowlist, the diff-or-die frontmatter gate, an isolated branch-commit posture, and the append-only audit log — rather than inventing a parallel write path.
A proposal's target allowlist is a required argument passed explicitly to the guard for every path before any branch exists, so a change cannot reach outside the scope its caller declared.
Every file in a multi-file proposal is gated in memory first so any abort raises before a branch is created, which is what guarantees a failed proposal never leaves a partial or orphan branch behind.
A proposal whose files all already match their content at HEAD returns a no-op with no branch and no pull request.

The queue has two tiers: a proposal in which every change is a new file in a free-append zone commits straight to HEAD on a fast path, which is what makes frictionless capture possible, while any curated path can never reach that fast path and the fast path never overwrites an existing file.

Caller-supplied proposal titles are reduced to a bounded restricted character set with traversal sequences removed and no leading dash or slash, so a title cannot inject a git option or ref traversal into the branch or pull-request commands.
A global proposal budget bounds the cold-start pull-request flood and is charged only when a real proposal branch is created, so no-ops and re-proposals cost nothing against the cap.
With no pull-request creation hook available the proposal still produces a local branch and diff with the pull request skipped, so the proposal is resumable later rather than lost.
Re-proposing the same slug reconciles the existing branch rather than creating a duplicate one.

Every generated artifact carries both machine-readable generated_by frontmatter, forced in by the renderer so a caller cannot omit it, and a rendered human-visible managed-block marker with an explicit end marker — so a generated file is unmistakable even in a reader view where frontmatter is collapsed.

The visible managed-block marker states that edits inside its region are overwritten, which makes the overwritable region explicit so a human edit inside it is never a surprise, and the frontmatter marker is what lets memory control classify a note as generated rather than guessing.

Salience scores each indexed note from graph link degree normalized by the vault maximum, embedding centrality as mean cosine to other notes, and rank-normalized write recency, combined with fixed weights and sorted deterministically with the path as a stable tiebreak.

Salience recency means recency of write rather than of access, because the audit log is write-only and adding a read signal would conflict with the read-only-is-structural posture; a note never written through the log scores zero and is dormant by definition.

Salience ensures full embedding coverage before computing centrality and reports a coverage_complete flag that is false when the embedder was unavailable or failed mid-fill, so a partial centrality is labelled rather than presented as final.

The digest surfaces salient-but-dormant notes ranked by structural importance alone — link degree and centrality, deliberately excluding recency because recency is what makes them dormant — and says so plainly when nothing is dormant rather than padding the list.

No salience field is ever written into a source note's frontmatter; the ranking exists only inside the generated digest note, because writing scores back into sources is exactly the churn the generated-artifact rules forbid.

A connection candidate is a pair whose cosine similarity clears a threshold and which no wikilink edge already joins, and the surface is kept high-precision by a near-duplicate exclusion at the top end — since shared templates, raw captures, and boilerplate reach near-identical similarity without being insight — plus a per-run cap and a deterministic sort.
When nothing clears the connection thresholds the surface returns nothing at all rather than emitting an empty proposal, so it never generates noise.

Connection suggestions are derived from stored note vectors and existing wikilink edges rather than from LLM knowledge-graph extraction, and when vectors come from the index a full unbudgeted embed runs first so a genuine pair is never missed because a note's chunks were unembedded.
A suggested connection is never written as an edge into a source note; it is rendered into a batched generated suggestions note offered as a proposal.

The navigation surface emits a Map-of-Content note and a metadata-driven dashboard view configuration as one proposal, both landing in a non-protected dashboards directory rather than a guard-protected one, and the dashboard needs no plugin code because it reads note metadata.

Navigation idempotency rides on a content-hash slug: identical content produces an identical slug so re-proposing an unchanged surface is a no-op, while changed content produces a new slug and a fresh proposal.

Navigation generation includes links to the salience digest and connection surfaces only when they are supplied, so it degrades gracefully and never blocks on an upstream surface that has not been generated.

The daily review composes the capture backlog with triage stages, recent audit-log writes, links to existing generated surfaces, recall-mode reminders including resolving before wikilinking and not guessing on null, degraded state, and cleanup actions with their commands, organized around the capture-to-cleanup loop.

The daily review explicitly does not move, delete, or rewrite any source note: it is a review-gated dashboard proposal over existing primitives, and every change it points at remains a separate previewed owner-driven action.
